title: Multi-Relay Cooperative Relaying: Lagrangian Power Allocation (DF Relays) — Exam Revision with Worked Example
description: Exam revision of the Lagrangian model for multi-relay decode-and-forward cooperative relaying: system model, two-hop bottleneck SNR, rate expression, Lagrangian formulation, SNR balancing, relay selection metric g_i, closed-form optimal powers, and the two-relay worked example solved step by step.

scenes.title: The power allocation problem
lines: A source has a fixed power budget, and several relays it could use. How much power should go to the source, and how much to each relay?
This is the Lagrangian model for multi relay cooperative relaying: an extended power allocation optimization, for decode and forward relays.
By the end, you will solve the exam style two relay example yourself.

scenes.title: System model
lines: The system model.
Source S communicates with destination D through M relays, R1 to RM.
The relays are decode and forward, and half duplex.
Each relay i has two channel gains: h_sri from source to relay, and h_rid from relay to destination.
Powers: Ps at the source, and Pri at relay i.
And the total power constraint: Ps plus the sum of all Pri must be at most P_total.

scenes.title: Rate expression: the two-hop bottleneck
lines: The rate expression.
Each relay creates a two hop path, and the path is only as good as its weaker hop.
So SNR_i equals the minimum of Ps h_sri over N0, and Pri h_rid over N0.
The destination combines the relayed signals by max min, or selection: R equals one half log2 of one plus the maximum over i of SNR_i.
The one half is because of the two half duplex time slots.
The objective: allocate Ps and every Pri to maximize R.

scenes.title: Lagrangian formulation
lines: The Lagrangian formulation.
Let t_i be the target SNR across the hops of relay i.
The constraints are: Ps h_sri over N0 is at least t_i, so the first hop reaches the target.
Pri h_rid over N0 is at least t_i, so the second hop reaches it too.
And Ps plus the sum of Pri is at most P_total.
The Lagrangian is L equals one half log2 of one plus the max of t_i, minus the multiplier weighted constraints.

scenes.title: Optimality: balanced SNR per active relay
lines: What does the optimum look like?
Think about it: if one hop had more SNR than the other, that extra power is wasted, because the minimum decides the rate.
So for every selected relay, in the active set A, the two hops are balanced: Ps h_sri equals Pri h_rid.
Rearranging: Pri equals Ps times h_sri over h_rid.
Put that into the total power: Ps plus the sum over active relays of Ps times h_sri over h_rid equals P_total.
Solve this for Ps, then get each Pri.

scenes.title: Relay selection rule
lines: But which relays should be active? The relay selection rule.
For each relay, compute the bottleneck metric g_i equals h_sri times h_rid, divided by h_sri plus h_rid.
This is like two resistors in parallel. It is small if either hop is weak.
A larger g_i means a better balanced two hop path.
Select the top k relays, typically k equals one or two, for power allocation.

scenes.title: Closed-form optimal powers
lines: Now the closed form optimal powers for the active relays.
Factor Ps out of the power equation: Ps times one plus the sum of h_sri over h_rid equals P_total.
So Ps equals P_total divided by one plus the sum over active relays of h_sri over h_rid.
And each Pri equals Ps times h_sri over h_rid.
These two formulas are all you need in the exam.

scenes.title: Worked example: two relays
lines: The worked example. P_total equals one, and N0 equals one.
Relay one: h_s1 equals 0.5, and h_1d equals 2.
Relay two: h_s2 equals 0.3, and h_2d equals 0.7.
Step one: compute g for each relay. g_1 equals 0.5 times 2, which is 1, divided by 0.5 plus 2, which is 2.5. So g_1 equals 0.4.
g_2 equals 0.3 times 0.7, which is 0.21, divided by 0.3 plus 0.7, which is 1. So g_2 equals 0.21.
Since 0.4 is greater than 0.21, choose relay one.
Step two: the ratio h_s1 over h_1d is 0.5 over 2, which is 0.25.
So Ps equals 1 divided by 1 plus 0.25, which is 1 over 1.25, equals 0.8.
Step three: P1 equals Ps times 0.25, which is 0.8 times 0.25, equals 0.2.
Check the total: 0.8 plus 0.2 equals 1. The budget is used exactly.

scenes.title: Check: are the hops balanced?
lines: Let us verify the balance.
Hop one SNR: Ps times h_s1 over N0 is 0.8 times 0.5, which is 0.4.
Hop two SNR: P1 times h_1d over N0 is 0.2 times 2, which is also 0.4. Balanced!
So the end to end SNR is 0.4, and the rate is one half log2 of 1.4, about 0.24 bits per second per hertz.
Notice the intuition: relay one has a very strong second hop, so it needs only a little power. Most of the budget goes to the source, whose hop is weaker.

scenes.title: Cooperative transmission diagrams
lines: The deck also shows cooperative transmission diagrams.
Cooperative transmission exploits the broadcast nature of wireless. Relays act as a virtual antenna of the source, like MIMO, giving multi user and multi route diversity.
In phase one, the sender transmits to the destination and the relay. In phase two, the relay forwards to the destination.
In the relay triangle, S sends to R over h_SR and to D over h_SD in time slot one. R sends to D over h_RD in time slot two.
In cooperative communication, the source's transmitted signal reaches both the relay and the destination, and the relay sends a retransmitted signal to the destination.

scenes.title: Summary and exam recipe
lines: Summary.
Multi relay DF optimization reduces to balancing the SNR on each hop.
Use the relay quality metric g_i for selection.
Closed form power allocation is available for the active relays.

Exam recipe: compute g_i for each relay. Pick the largest. Compute the ratio h_sr over h_rd. Ps equals P_total over one plus the ratio sum. Each relay power is Ps times its ratio. Then check the total.
Good luck in your exam!
